author: Kuber Sharma (@kubersharmax)
description: Scores a prospect’s data-stack readiness for zero-copy, agentic GTM. This measures architectural readiness only. It is NOT an ICP fit assessment: a strong-fit account can score low because its stack is legacy, and a poor-fit account can score high because its stack is modern. Use it alongside ICP scoring, never instead of it.

onion_layers.name: Legacy ETL Dependency
onion_layers.description: Prospect relies on scheduled batch ETL for core data movement. Indicates deep legacy middleware investment.

onion_layers.name: Middleware Lock-In
onion_layers.description: Prospect is entrenched in heavyweight middleware that resists zero-copy patterns.

onion_layers.name: Manual Data Wrangling
onion_layers.description: Data movement depends on human-in-the-loop manual steps rather than automated activation.

onion_layers.name: Siloed Data Governance
onion_layers.description: Data access is bureaucratically gated, making real-time activation impossible.

onion_layers.name: Legacy CRM/MAP Fragmentation
onion_layers.description: GTM stack uses legacy or fragmented CRM/MAP integrations that resist modern data activation.

zero_copy_readiness_signals.name: Cloud-Native Data Platform
zero_copy_readiness_signals.description: Warehouse is the source of truth. This is the precondition for everything else.

zero_copy_readiness_signals.name: Warehouse-Native Activation (transitional)
zero_copy_readiness_signals.description: Reverse-ETL tooling (Census, Hightouch, RudderStack) is a TRANSITIONAL signal, not a zero-copy endpoint. It shows the prospect has already centralised on the warehouse as source of truth, which is the hard part. It still moves copies of data out to the CRM or MAP, which the playbook identifies as the ETL tax. Weighted low deliberately: readiness to adopt zero-copy, not evidence of it.

scope_note: Readiness is not fit. Combine with your ICP model before routing or disqualifying any account.
signal_hierarchy: In-situ query and compute against the warehouse is the endpoint. Event-driven and composable-CDP patterns are strong intermediate signals. Reverse ETL is transitional: better than batch ETL, still not zero-copy. Legacy batch ETL and heavyweight middleware are the penalised layers.
